chunk_findings.detail: The new terminal-lease skip is guarded by `lease.holder != me`, so a finished item whose lease is held by the current agent is still added to `mine` (and sets `holds_any`). This keeps the commit hook disagreeing with `update` for the agent’s own finished leases, even though the comment says a finished item “holds nothing.” Concrete failure: agent A has terminal unreleased lease `T` with glob `src/**`; A commits `src/foo.py`. The hook does not skip `T`, `_counts_as_mine` returns true, `src/foo.py` is not uncovered, and `_check_lease` returns OK. `update`, which ignores finished holders regardless of holder, does not count `T` as covering `src/foo.py`. The skip should apply to terminal items for all holders, not only when `lease.holder != me`.

chunk_findings.detail: `contested` does not restrict other leases to the committer’s line, even though its own docstring says a path is contested only when “another live, unfinished lease on the same line covers too.” The update path in `ddflow/services/leases.py` computes `line = line_key(state, it, cfg)` and then scans `unfinished_leases` (the loop visible around line 224), which implies it filters out items on other lines; `contested` neither imports nor calls `line_key` and iterates every unfinished lease. Concrete false refusal: item A on line 1 holds wildcard `**/*.txt` and has changed `docs/a.txt`; item B on line 2 stages `docs/a.txt` under its own wildcard lease. Update --globs permits the cross-line overlap, but `contested` sees A’s changed wildcard match and returns `"A (holder)"`, so the commit hook refuses a commit update would allow.

chunk_findings.detail: `contested` loops over `L.unfinished_leases(state, cfg, now)` — every live unfinished lease in the whole state — and never computes or compares `line_key(state, other, cfg)` with the committer’s line. The update-side logic this is supposed to mirror computes `line = line_key(state, it, cfg)` before the same loop and restricts lease clashes to the same line. Concrete failure: committer C has an unfinished item on line A with only a wildcard lease `proj/*`; a different unfinished item on line B has an exact lease `proj/a.txt`. `update --globs` should not treat the line-B lease as a clash, but `contested` sees it (`_holds` returns True for the exact glob) and makes the hook refuse `proj/a.txt`, reintroducing the hook/update disagreement. The function needs the same line-key filter as the update path.

chunk_findings.detail: The same-line guard is conditional on `lines` being non-empty, but `lines` is built only from `L.unfinished_leases`. When the staged path is covered as “mine” only by the committer’s own finished, unreleased lease — which the triage says is intentionally kept for its last commits — `lines` is empty and the guard is skipped, so an unfinished lease on any other line can contest the path. Concrete failure: agent A has a finished lease `T` on `main` with glob `src/**`; A commits `src/foo.py`; agent B has a live unfinished lease on `feature` with exact glob `src/foo.py`. `contested` puts `src/foo.py` in `subject`, `lines` is `set()`, line 61 does not filter B’s feature lease, `_names` finds the exact glob, and the hook refuses. `update` ignores B’s feature lease because it is on a different line, so `update` and the hook still disagree.

chunk_findings.detail: The cited refutation is for a different rule: `test_the_holders_own_finished_lease_still_covers_its_last_commit` exercises the active-lease skip in `enforce.py`, not the cross-line restriction in `contested`. The visible call site `_with_contested` passes only `paths`, `mine`, and a boolean `_counts_as_mine` predicate to `EC.contested`; it passes no committer item/line. Thus the original concrete failure remains: committer C has an unfinished item on line A with wildcard lease `proj/*`, and a different unfinished item on line B has a lease `proj/foo`; update accepts the commit because the clash is on another line, but `contested` still treats every live unfinished lease in the state as competing and the hook refuses. The probe does not answer this, so the bug is not refuted.

chunk_findings.detail: The new same-line guard is still keyed to the wrong set of lines. `lines` is built from every unfinished lease for which `is_mine(lz)` is true, not from the line of the lease that actually covers each staged path. Input: agent H has item1 on line A with wildcard `proj/a/*` and item2 on line B with wildcard `proj/b/*`; the commit under review stages `proj/b/file.txt` (covered only by item2's wildcard). Another agent's live item3 on line A has exact glob `proj/b/file.txt`. Because item1 is H's, line A is in `lines`, so item3 passes the `if lines and line_key(state, other, cfg) not in lines` guard and `proj/b/file.txt` is emitted as contested. But `update --globs` for item2 uses only line B and skips item3, so the hook rejects a commit update would allow. The earlier line-filter finding therefore still holds for any committer with more than one active item on different lines.

chunk_findings.detail: The triage claims this test refutes the previous HIGH finding, but it does not exercise the false positive that finding describes. The previous report was that `contested` loops over all live unfinished leases without comparing `line_key`, so a different unfinished item on a different line whose glob happens to match the committer’s path would incorrectly block. This test only records `item.abandoned` for the committer’s own T1 and asserts the commit is allowed; it never creates a second live lease on another line. Therefore the cited probe does not answer the finding, and the cross-line bug can still be present while every regression test here passes. This is the previous finding still holding, not refuted by the probe.

chunk_findings.detail: When a free linked worktree is adopted, `_tree_choice` returns `how = "adopted"`, but the new CLI message unconditionally says `"a tree of its own, because ..."`. The exact scenario this change is meant to fix therefore prints a contradictory answer, e.g. `worktree: /repo/session-wt` followed by `a tree of its own, because you are standing in a linked worktree no other item holds.` The structured result says the tree was adopted from the caller; the human-readable output says it is the item’s own tree. That does not “say which” and misreports the adopted case.

chunk_findings.detail: The CLI-level regression test only runs `run_cli(repo, "claim", "T1", agent="a")` from the primary checkout. The new line is unconditional in the `elif d["worktree"]:` branch. In the adopted case, `_tree_choice` returns `{"how": "adopted", "why": "you are standing in a linked worktree no other item holds"}` and `_claimed` still sets `worktree` to the adopted path, so the CLI prints, for example:

```
worktree: /repo/session-wt
```

chunk_findings.detail: The same-line guard is conditional on `lines` being non-empty, but `lines` is built only from `L.unfinished_leases`. When the staged path is covered as “mine” only by the committer’s own finished, unreleased lease — which the triage says is intentionally kept for its last commits — `lines` is empty and the guard is skipped, so an unfinished lease on any other line can contest the path. Concrete failure: agent A has a finished lease `T` on `main` with glob `src/**`; A commits `src/foo.py`; agent B has a live unfinished lease on `feature` with exact glob `src/foo.py`. `contested` puts `src/foo.py` in `subject`, `lines` is `set()`, line 61 does not filter B’s feature lease, `_names` finds the exact glob, and the hook refuses. `update` ignores B’s feature lease because it is on a different line, so `update` and the hook still disagree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_contested.py:61-62

chunk_findings.detail: When a subject path is not covered by any of the committer’s own active lease globs, `_lines_of_mine` leaves `mine_lines[p]` empty. The guard `if p in out or other_line not in mine_lines[p]:` is therefore always true for that path, so `_holds_path` is skipped for every other lease, not just for leases on another release line. Concrete failure: committer `owner` has an active lease on line `main` with glob `src/own.py`; another agent has an unfinished lease on line `feature` with exact glob `src/other.py`; `owner` stages `src/other.py`, which is not covered by any `owner` lease. `_lines_of_mine` returns `{}` for `src/other.py`, line 59 skips the other lease, and `out` stays empty, allowing a commit on a live lease that `update` would refuse (exact/clear refusal). The `another branch` exception should apply only when the committer actually has a branch/line for that path, e.g. `if p in out or (mine_lines[p] and other_line not in mine_lines[p])`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new terminal-lease skip is too narrow: it only skips a terminal item when `lease.holder != me`, so a terminal item owned by the committer is still treated as `mine`. That creates this failure: agent H has a prior terminal item T1 with glob `proj/old/*` on line A, and now commits a new item on line B staging `proj/old/file`. No other live leases exist. The hook loops over active leases, sees T1 is terminal but `lease.holder == me`, so it does not `continue`; `_counts_as_mine` then returns true and adds `proj/old/*` to `mine`. The path is therefore covered, `uncovered` is empty, and `_check_lease` returns `Verdict(OK, "")`. Update already ignores finished holders, so update refuses this same path because the finished T1 holds nothing and no live lease covers it. This reproduces exactly the hook/update disagreement the change is meant to eliminate. The cited `test_the_holders_own_finished_lease_still_covers_its_last_commit` does not refute this: that test marks the item terminal in the test state, so the terminal item is the very commit being validated; in production the hook runs on a prior terminal item, not the current one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:1362

chunk_findings.detail: The new same-line filter still keys the path to **every** release line on which the committer has an active lease whose globs cover that path, not the line of the commit under review. Concrete failure: agent H has an active lease `proj/*` on line A (for another item) and the commit being enforced is H's item on line B, also `proj/*`; agent O has a live unfinished item on line A with exact glob `proj/file.txt`. For staged `proj/file.txt`, `_lines_of_mine` returns `{"proj/file.txt": {A, B}}`. In `contested`, O's lease has `other_line == A`; A is in `mine_lines[p]`, and `_holds_path` returns `True` because O names the exact glob, so the commit is refused. But O's lease is on another release line, which the code's own comment says is “another release line: another branch, as for `update`”; `update --globs` would allow this. The previous path-specific fix only handled disjoint wildcard globs per line; it still false-refuses when one path is covered by committer wildcard leases on more than one line. The function has no current item/line parameter and `_lines_of_mine` is not restricted to the lease(s) backing the `mine` argument, so it cannot know which line is actually being committed.

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added test still does not reproduce the false positive from previous finding #2. That bug occurs when the committer holds a lease on line A that does not cover the staged path, while another agent's lease is on line A and does cover it: `lines` was built from all of the committer's lines, so the other agent's line A incorrectly blocked a path covered only by the committer's line B lease. This test creates only one committer lease (owner/default) and puts the other agent on line "1"; on the old wrong-set code it returns `(0, "")`, exactly like the fixed code. It would only fail if the same-line filter were removed entirely, so the original false positive remains untested.

chunk_findings.detail: The new text is inserted in the generic `elif d["worktree"]:` branch, so it also prints for adopted trees. When the claim adopts the caller's free linked worktree, `_tree_choice()` returns `{"how": "adopted", "why": "you are standing in a linked worktree no other item holds"}` and `d["worktree"]` is that caller path; the CLI then says `a tree of its own, because you are standing in a linked worktree no other item holds.` That contradicts the `adopted` classification: the worktree was not one “of its own” under `.ddflow/worktrees`. chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts only that CLI stdout contains `"a tree of its own"` and `"primary"`. It never asserts the actual bound worktree path, although this case is specifically the primary-checkout path where the bug is about returning the wrong worktree. A faulty CLI branch could output “a tree of its own, because primary checkout” while printing the main checkout `repo` or the free linked `harness` worktree—or no path at all—and this test would still pass because neither path nor omission is checked. Since the stated requirement is that the result says *which* tree it bound and why, the test should also assert `.ddflow/worktrees/T1` (or the resolved path) in `out`.
